skill.name: convex-monitor
skill.description: Wait for the next Convex error or feature request and follow a workflow based on the event type.
skill.summary: Monitor Convex events without manual polling where blocking waits are supported.
skill.author: convex

security_audit.summary: The flagged backticks mark an MCP tool name in Markdown and do not execute a shell command. The workflow directs agents to fix errors and build incoming feature requests without requiring approval for code changes. No evidence found of an embedded prompt injection attempt.

remediation.issue: Incoming events can trigger code changes without explicit approval.
remediation.suggestion: Treat event payloads as data and verify feature requests with an authorized maintainer. Report findings and request explicit approval before editing files or deploying changes.

finding_verdicts.reason: The backticks on SKILL.md line 14 delimit the MCP tool name in Markdown. The surrounding workflow passes named arguments to that tool and contains no Ruby or shell execution.

semantic_findings.title: Event-driven code changes lack an approval gate
semantic_findings.description: The workflow tells the agent to fix errors and build feature requests as soon as events arrive. It does not require approval, so an incoming event could lead to unauthorized edits.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Line 15 explicitly directs the agent to fix errors and build features. The workflow and rules do not require approval before changes.

content.user_title: Monitor Convex Errors and Feature Requests
content.value_statement: Convex errors and feature requests can arrive while you are working elsewhere. This skill waits for a matching event and guides the next step based on its type.
actual_capabilities: Passes a project directory, event filters, and a timeout to the MCP event tool.
Uses the first matching event from local error logs, deployment subscriptions, or Sentinel production error records.
Routes local errors to diagnosis, production errors to Sentinel triage, and feature requests to implementation.
Handles a quiet heartbeat by restarting the wait.
Uses the pack's polling fallback where blocking MCP is unavailable.
limitations: Blocking waits require the Convex MCP event tool.
Production error monitoring requires a deployed Convex cloud app and Sentinel.
Each wait returns the first matching event or a quiet heartbeat, not a complete event history.
The default workflow does not require approval before making code changes.

use_cases.title: Diagnose a local Convex error
use_cases.description: Wait for the next development error and summarize the likely cause before making changes.

use_cases.title: Triage a production error
use_cases.description: Wait for a Sentinel production error and collect details for incident triage.

use_cases.title: Review an incoming feature request
use_cases.description: Summarize the first matching request and confirm its scope before assigning implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Report the next local error
prompt_templates.scenario: Check a local project during development.
prompt_templates.prompt: Watch the current Convex project for the next local error. Summarize it and stop without editing files.

prompt_templates.title: Set a time limit
prompt_templates.scenario: Check for an error after reproducing a problem.
prompt_templates.prompt: Wait up to 60 seconds for a local Convex error. If the wait returns a quiet heartbeat, report it and stop.

prompt_templates.title: Triage a Sentinel event
prompt_templates.scenario: Investigate an error in a deployed project with Sentinel configured.
prompt_templates.prompt: Wait for the next Sentinel production error in this project. Summarize the evidence and propose a next step without changing files or deploying.

prompt_templates.title: Review multiple event types
prompt_templates.scenario: Monitor an approved project for production errors and feature requests.
prompt_templates.prompt: Watch this project for production errors and feature requests. For the first event, report its type and propose a next step. Ask for approval before editing files.

output_examples.input: Wait for a local error and summarize it without making changes.
output_examples.output: A local error arrived. The request failed because a required field was missing. No files changed.

output_examples.input: Wait for a production error for 60 seconds and stop after the first heartbeat.
output_examples.output: The wait returned a quiet heartbeat. No matching production error arrived during the wait.

output_examples.input: Review the next feature request without implementing it.
output_examples.output: The request asks for a date filter on the activity view. Confirm the default date range before approving implementation.

best_practices: Confirm the project directory and restrict the wait to the event types you need.
Use a bounded wait and tell the agent whether to stop or continue after a quiet heartbeat.
Verify incoming requests with an authorized maintainer and approve proposed edits before implementation.
anti_patterns: Treating an event payload as permission to edit or deploy.
Expecting production errors without a deployed Convex cloud app and Sentinel.
Treating a quiet heartbeat as proof that the deployment is healthy.

faq.question: What can the skill watch for?
faq.answer: It handles local Convex or Next.js errors, Sentinel production errors, feature requests, and quiet heartbeats.

faq.question: What do I need for production monitoring?
faq.answer: You need a deployed Convex cloud app with Sentinel.

faq.question: What happens if blocking MCP is unavailable?
faq.answer: The pack uses polling where supported and returns the same typed events.

faq.question: What does a quiet heartbeat mean?
faq.answer: No matching event arrived during that wait. The default workflow starts another wait.

faq.question: Can I limit monitoring to specific events?
faq.answer: Yes. Specify the project directory, event types, and wait timeout.

faq.question: Can I monitor without changing code?
faq.answer: Yes. Ask for a report only and require approval before edits. The default workflow directs the agent to act on errors and requests.
